headline: Gujarat Gas Limited announces Record Date 3 under Scheme of Arrangement
sum: Gujarat Gas Limited intimated shareholders of Record Date 3 under a Scheme of Arrangement, signalling a material corporate restructuring with multi-tranche approval and execution mechanics typical of NCLT-sanctioned schemes involving slump sales, mergers or demergers.
implication: The reference to 'Record Date 3' indicates a phased scheme implementation requiring sequential shareholder record dates—a precedent-setting feature suggesting either a multi-leg slump/merger, or a demerger with staggered entitlements, and signals completion of earlier regulatory (likely NCLT and stock exchange) approvals.
detail: Gujarat Gas Limited, a major downstream gas distribution and petrochemicals entity, notified shareholders of the third record date associated with an ongoing Scheme of Arrangement. The company did not disclose counterparty identities, consideration or merger/slump terms in this public notice; however, the invocation of Record Date 3 confirms that at least two prior record dates have been executed, and implies NCLT sanction and stock exchange in-principle approval were obtained in prior months. This multi-date structure is typical of complex schemes involving asset demergers, inter-company transfers or multi-tranche consideration.

framework.note: Scheme of Arrangement: approval by Tribunal (NCLT), sanction by court, and creditor/member consent—central to validity and enforceability.
Procedural framework for Scheme filings, advertising, shareholder voting and Tribunal sanctioning orders.

framework.ref: SEBI Listing Rules, 2015, Regulation 30 & Schedule III
framework.note: Mandatory disclosure and record date notification to stock exchanges; exchange approval of scheme-related corporate actions.
Tax-neutral treatment of slump sales under schemes (if applicable); may exempt scheme-related transfers from capital gains tax.

framework.ref: NSE/BSE Listing Agreement & Circulars on Schemes
framework.note: Exchange-specific guidance on scheme announcements, record dates, delisting (if merger involves listed target) and shareholder communication.
If scheme involves distressed asset transfer or creditor haircut, IBC framework may apply; confirm scheme does not trigger IBC moratorium.
If counterparty or consideration structure involves foreign investment or overseas asset transfer, FEMA approval may be required.

framework.ref: Petroleum Rules / Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL) Regulations
framework.note: Gas distribution and infrastructure assets may require sector-specific approvals from PNGRB or GAIL; confirm no regulatory objection.

conditions: NCLT sanction of the Scheme (completed or in-flight; not disclosed)
Stock exchange in-principle approval and filing (completed)
Execution of Record Date 3 condition precedent (shareholder entitlement vesting)
approvals: NCLT approval and Court sanction (inferred as completed, given multi-record-date execution)
NSE/BSE listing compliance and record date certification
Shareholder approval (assumed at or before Record Date 1)
structure.novel: Multi-tranche record date structure (Record Date 3) suggests either a phased demerger with staggered share issuance, or a slump sale with deferred entitlements—uncommon in single-leg M&A, signalling complexity in asset separation or consideration settlement.

triggers.note: Core regulatory gate; scheme must be sanctioned by NCLT and approved by creditors/members per statutory thresholds.

triggers.law: SEBI Listing Rules Reg. 30 & Schedule III
triggers.note: Record date announcement and shareholder notification mandatory within two days of board approval.
Exchange-specific eligibility and timing rules for scheme-related record dates and share credit.
Gas distribution or production assets may require regulator consent to change control or asset transfer.
